snippet.title: Google Ask Me Anything - Part 3
snippet.description:
The third and final part of the Google Ask Me Anything series! I hope that this Q&A sheds a lot of light about what it's like to work as a Software Engineer at Google and general life at Google.

Part 1 of this AMA: https://youtu.be/TWsx9CouEZE
Part 2 of this AMA: https://youtu.be/7DeP4Xlw4Po
Why I Don't Have Impostor Syndrome: https://youtu.be/JnZvhzAX9IE

0:00 | Introduction
0:51 | Did you Google at Google?
0:53 | Do I think working at Google is overrated?
1:29 | How much experience do you need to work on some of Google’s main products like Google Search or Gmail?
1:53 | Is all the food at Google free?
2:04 | What was the youngest age of a Google Software Engineer that I saw?
2:41 | Does the work at Google become monotonous?
3:42 | Can someone with a not-so-great college but with ample time crack the Google interview? If yes, does Google only require algorithm-style questions that anyone can do with repetitive learning?
4:25 | Are the Google perks all that they’re made out to be? Did I get bored of them after a while?
5:20 | What’s the process for getting a raise? Do you have to explicitly ask for one, or do you get one after a certain number of good performance reviews?
6:54 | How long does it take to get comfortable with Google’s development environment?
7:07 | How many people did I work with who were incompetent?
7:42 | Do frontend developers at Google use Angular or anything else?
8:16 | How many meetings are in person and how many meetings are on Hangouts?
8:50 | Did I ever suffer from impostor syndrome while at Google?
9:00 | Is it normal to make as much money as I did working at Google when I had little to no experience?
9:32 | Is it true that you only learn Google-specific technologies and skills that have little to no carryover in the “real” world while working at Google?
10:39 | Is the free food at Google really tasty?
11:08 | Is there any realistic chance of someone without a degree becoming a Software Engineer at Google?
11:17 | Does age matter in the recruitment process at Google, or is it only skill that matters?
11:24 | Get a life.
11:26 | What’s the difference between the NYC office and the Bay Area offices? Can Googlers change locations (within a country or even to another country)?
12:10 | What surprised me the most about working at Google?
13:53 | In all honesty, how hard is the work at Google?
14:50 | What did I work during my last week at Google?!
15:25 | How easy is it to get a promotion, and is there an established pathway to do so?
16:23 | What was the most stressful day I ever worked at Google like?
16:59 | What the hell do Google engineers do and does the average Joe have access to more information about projects than exactly what they need for what they’re working on?
17:22 | Do the Google offices have a room to sleep, to work out, to play games, and to relax?
17:37 | How does a Google Software Engineer get “readability” in a programming language?
19:12 | Do all project managers at Google have a technical background?
19:31 | Did I ever have a sneak peek at the FooBar Challenge source code?
19:36 | What is it like being exclusively a frontend developer? Is it perceived as “equal” to being a backend developer?
20:04 | Is it true that Google has gotten so big that its culture has morphed into a bureaucratic-like environment similar to many big corporations?
20:59 | Can I describe the Google offices that I visited?
21:43 | What are my thoughts one the Engineering Residency program?
22:20 | Conclusion

snippet.title: Working At Google - Ask Me Anything - Part 2
snippet.description:
Ever wondered what it's like to work at Google? In this video, I answer a bunch of your questions about life as a software engineer at Google and working as a Google software engineer.

Part 1 of this Q&A: https://youtu.be/TWsx9CouEZE
A Day in the Life of a Google Software Engineer: https://youtu.be/oHBFD8cfXho
How Often Do Software Engineers Write Algorithms: https://youtu.be/Pb9UNhfy1U4

0:00 | Introduction
0:28 | If I were the CEO of Google, what (if anything) would I try to change about Google’s culture in order to give those who work there an even better experience?
2:26 | Once you leave Google or Facebook, how hard is it to go back? Do you have to go through the interview process again?
4:21 | How much did I know going in the job vs. how much did I learn on the job (things like in-depth knowledge of technologies and frameworks)?
5:54 | How do you land a new job (without your current boss knowing) while being employed? Are there conditions in your job contract regarding trade secrets? 
8:01 | Did I ever use the algorithms and design skills that we teach on AlgoExpert and SystemsExpert while on the job, and do Google engineers use the command line and Stack Overflow?
9:43 | What are some of Google’s “magical” internal tools in comparison to popular tools used outside of Google?
12:38 | Did I encounter software engineers at Google who were still “on the learning curve” (i.e., who weren’t geniuses)?
14:01 | How much time do Googlers have for one small-scale project?
14:23 | What did my work schedule look like and how much time did I spend coding?
14:35 | Would I say that the Perf (performance) process is more political than anything else?
15:36 | How easy is it to change functions internally (like from Software Engineer to Product Manager)?
16:56 | What if a Noogler performs terribly during the first few months at Google?
17:48 | What did I do for my 20% project (plus general insights about 20% projects)?
20:10 | Do most software engineers at Google have a good amount of work experience? Are there a lot of new grads and junior engineers?
20:57 | What does a Staff Software Engineer do?
21:02 | What are people’s social lives like at Google? How do people make friends, and are friendships formed in the workplace? How easily so?
22:16 | How do your seniors react if you ever commit buggy code?
22:23 | If you get an offer from Google, but you’re from another country or city than the office you’ll be in, does Google provide you with housing?
22:57 | The moment you’ve all been waiting for…
23:20 | Can you request equipment like a new laptop, extra monitors, luxury keyboards, etc.?
23:48 | The continuation of the moment you’ve all been waiting for… Given the same compensation and location, which would be better for early career: an L3 SWE role at Google or an E3 SWE role at Facebook?
25:46 | Conclusion
